success.description: Sections2.2–2.3 Steps6–8 give an author-rounded expected wrong96-bit-assignment count of about2^-34.5 per64-bit terminal-key pass. Markov's inequality and a union bound over the two complementary passes give the displayed conditional full-key lower-bound estimate. Backward expansion of the complete AES128 terminal key returns the master key. The approximation sign preserves the source rounding: this is not a rigorous numerical bound for actual fixed-query AES. The source uses effective≈2^28.5 useful pairs per tested terminal-half hypothesis in each pass, not certified integer counts. For explanatory integer N lower-bounding every such count across both passes, its unrounded conditional model is max(0,1-2^97(1-2^-22)^N); N is not a new tunable assignment or cost(N) family. Across-pair survival and q≈2^-22 are inherited source heuristics; no independence between different wrong assignments or the two passes is required. Step8 already prices both passes. This describes the intended impossible-relation model, not a repair of disputed literal ShiftRows/final-MixColumns coordinates or restricted-input probabilities. Useful-pair acquisition at2^91.5 queries and hard-budget tails remain unquantified. All original conflicts and five local components remain unchanged.
